paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Josiah gave everything he had to the LORD, and he did it the way the Book said to do it. The writer says that neither before nor after him was there any king like him, who turned to the LORD "with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength, according to all the Law of Moses." (2 Kings 23:25) That's what the LORD looks for: a whole heart, and a life that follows His Word.

Now sit with the hard part, because the writer doesn't skip it. "Nevertheless, the LORD did not turn away from the fury of His burning anger," and the writer ties it to what Manasseh had done. (2 Kings 23:26) I think that stings, friend. It tells us Josiah's faithfulness didn't change what the LORD had already said about Judah. (2 Kings 23:27)

The story isn't over, and neither is the teaching. So here's what I'd carry out of my bakery today. Obey God's Word with your whole heart while you have the chance, and don't wait around for a reward to show up first. I've been tossed in a drawer and called out of it, and I'm telling you, a heart that stays faithful to the LORD is never wasted.
